english_verification.review_scope: Checked the current Mod's H14 opening history, English country name, representative flavour text, and mission route structure; read the related English Eordand timeline chunk for the later 1589, 1628, and 1713 claims. This was not a full mission or mechanics audit, and the native English national ideas were not retranscribed. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: No dedicated Eighard, Banoghard, or Bannoghard English Wiki page was available in the offline query; the timeline does not certify detailed national history or current mechanics.
The third-stage magical-project total cost, timers, and penalties were not fully audited.
The source article's historical ambush has no reliable year; no date was added.

rationale.campaign_length: 60 directly defined missions, including mutually exclusive routes, with a long unique branch.
rationale.colonization: Cold-region colonization and outpost development create real waiting periods.
rationale.complexity: Mutually exclusive mission sections, spell research, outposts, and cult counters interact.
rationale.dark_story: The pit imprisonment, death threats, and bone intimidation are explicit in the text.
rationale.difficulty: Resource and timing management are substantial; some project costs remain unverified and this is not a playtest assessment.
rationale.diplomacy: Former alliances and cult politics matter, although war is the stronger axis.
rationale.early_pressure: The Winter Court conflict and infrastructure preparation create pressure; this has not been quantified in play.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Warming rituals, the Cult of Rot, and special magical projects reshape the entire national route.
rationale.narrative_density: The crusade's collapse, restoration of status, cult seizure of power, and renaming form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Cities, mage towers, outposts, and research require development, but this is not a pure tall country.
rationale.trade_economy: Iron, ports, and facilities support the advance; trade is not the main route.
rationale.warfare: The northern crusade, Autumn Court rivalry, and later cross-regional expansion are the main loop.

identity.appearance: A 1444 Autumn Court theocracy with Tuathak culture and Darblath as capital; the Cult of Rot choice determines the mission route.
identity.formation_scope: H14's unique route can rename the same Tag to Liughagcal and Banoghard; without accepting Rot, it can instead meet general conditions to form H21 Eordand, change Tag, and replace the tree. The routes are mutually exclusive.
successors: H21 Eordand (a conditional formation detour, not a continuation of the Rot route)

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
The cold shores of the northern Fogharabh have long been a battleground between the Autumn and Winter Courts, but until the Hibernal Crusade only the city of Darblath and a few other possessions could remain under the hands of the Tuathak. Eighard stood as the bulwark of the Autumn Court against the unrelenting wintry winds for centuries, until matters of fate thrust them into greatness. Their hated enemies, the Snecboth, were lulled into a feeling of false safety, believing that they had nothing to fear from the Tuathak who cowered in their fortresses until the end of winter. Eighard developed a plan, gathering support from the old Autumn Court of Dorcurt and gathering a vast army of the faithful. A holy war to end the Winter once and for all was declared: once the Snecboth and their lands were conquered by Eighard and their allies, they could end their idolatry and cease the hated season forever!

The Hibernal Crusade won victory after victory, crushing the Winter Court and seizing the lands eastward towards what would become Jhorgashirr and Slegcal. All that remained was Gemradcurt, but the Esbagg of Eighard, Andrall Harvestcrown, knew that their allies would seize their conquered lands and sought to force their loyalty at Minnorac, the Field of Oaths. This proved to be a cataclysmic mistake, for they were ambushed there by the Strutmar Peitar and the unity of the Hibernal Crusade was shattered with the death of Esbagg Andrall Harvestcrown.

Following the ambush at Minnorac, the remaining leadership of the Hibernal Crusade rushed to consolidate power and seized control of the conquered lands, forming the traitorous states of Jhorgashirr and Slegcal. While Eigharders view them as deserters, they do not show this openly, and their government has maintained friendly relations with them in a vain attempt to regain the influence they once held.

description.text: Battered by the incessant frigid winds and waves, Darblath is a cold and mirthless place. Yet, it could be worse, for the hardships the Eigharders face have bestowed unto them unique spells and incantations. The traditional magical arts of the Autumn Court have been mastered and redefined: although all things must change like how the leaves change in the end of Autumn, perhaps it could be put off until later. The Warmth Rites were some of the first Eigharder spells, requiring intense and uninterrupted concentration by a team of no less than twelve druids. Over many years the Warmth Rites have acted as a ward against the cold, but have never been enough to keep old Winter at bay.

description.text: The second magical innovation of Eighard has permitted their Tuathak Legions to persist in the desolate northern wilderness. Only at the Icewardery of Darblath, a secluded building guarded far behind the Esbagg's fortress, are these enchantments prepared to ensure the exclusivity of their technique continues. Icewarded equipment often appear plain at first sight, no different from common armor, but beneath its surface are revealed a gleaming sheen on scratches or splinters. Donning icewarded equipment produces a warming effect on the wearer: while not enough to allow unlimited action in freezing temperatures, it is enough to permit Eighard's legions full ability to complete their complex and successful maneuvers.

description.text: The eternal struggle against the hated Winter has required an iron grip on all available resources, spurring the creation of the Hibernal Requisitions doctrine. During wartime, the Esbagg of Eighard may seize anything that is required for the war effort on the condition that the land or resource is returned or repaid, but any suspected cases of heresy will be dealt with harshly. When in Eighard it is wise to willingly surrender anything required for the Hibernal Requisition, as throughout its many years of usage almost all who refuse have been found and executed as Wintry informants.

description.text: The bleak weather of Darblath harbor is reflected in its chief export: muted gray, blue, and brown dyes. The boreal hinterlands provide a bountiful source of these dyes, crushed from bark and squeezed from soil in stinking vats. These muted colors have become a proud heritage of Eigharders, claiming that it shows their humility and practicality. However, they are quick to boast that their dyes are far superior, and more plentiful, than Sglard's foppish bright dyes, not to even mention the garish pink of Dearktir!

description.text: The backcountry roads, practically anywhere outside of Darblath and its immediate environs, are haunted by raiding Snecboth who threaten our very existence. Mobilizing the army against such threats is impractical, for they melt away into the frozen woods at the blink of an eye, and return just as quickly. To face such a threat the Boreal Vigilance Corps was established, composed of junior regiments that receive their training by patrolling the roadways.

description.text:
Unending strife and hatred over many generations is not conducive to creating a welcoming and friendly society. Unable to back down from war with the Wintry heretics, many in Eighard have taken to extreme measures to ensure victory. The Cult of Rot upholds the nature of decay of fallen Autumn leaves, viewing that as the ultimate and just punishment for those sentenced to execution. At first viewed as a troublesome but unimportant heretical cult by the mainstream Autumn Court who favor the aspect of Autumn as the season of harvest and preparation, the Cult of Rot seized control of Eighard overtime, slowly replacing the governorship until even their Esbagg adhered to their practices.

Their most infamous practice was the construction of a new prison in Darblath, a squat but deep building extending far into the earth, where heretics and prisoners were locked in pit-like cells and left until their body decayed into soil. The many bones left behind were showcased as a warning to would-be troublemakers, with some thrown into a massive pile outside the prison as example, and others left in a long corridor all over the floor and walls where domestic and foreign dignitaries were reminded of their fate should they fail.

description.text: Eordand united, the four seasons for the first time stride in unison. However, not all submit to our rule. In the hinterlands and even amongst our cities there are those who would dare question our authority, and wish for a return to the supremacy of one season. We must do all we can to stop these dissidents and preserve our union.

description.text: In the past the expeditions of the Eordan faith only retrieved Precursor artifacts from dangerous locations. In the present, further steps must be taken to secure our access to artifacts. All locations with possible Precursor artifacts must be fortified with the Eordan faith!

description.text: Zealots of the Eordellon faith, the Domandrod Lightbringers are those who spent years stalking the Domandrod with the Fey Lords themselves. These Lightbringers, thankfully, see us as the chosen heirs of Eordand, and will unfalteringly serve us. They will bring to the enemy death in sword, magic and shot.

description.text: Eordand is replete with Precursor ruins, many of them still somewhat intact. For centuries our people dwelt within these ruins, mere squatters compared to our majesty today. The Ruins are ruined no longer, restored to at least some semblance of their lost glory.

description.text: As one of the sole survivors of the Day of Ashen Skies, Eordand has returned from the grave. All around us the Ruinborn and Cannorians squabble over the land and the few ruins, but it is Eordand that are the true heirs to these lands. None shall hold us back from what is our destiny!

description.text: Despite the faltering of our neighbours, they are still our cousins. Be they the Ynnic, Alecandi or even the Cursed Ones, our brethren all need our protection from the Outsiders. The Eordan faith will protect them, and they will see the wisdom that comes from the seasons and the Fey.

description.text: Independent or parallel to the Cannorian artificery, Eordand channeled magic into items at power no less. With these inventions, our industries are far more efficient in all fields. Eordan products, even magirifles, should be shipped across the world, for it is best for others to be dependent on us.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this if you dislike colonial and spell-research waits or do not want a dark route involving prisoner treatment and cult terror.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Organize the Autumn Court war and cold-weather administration first; prepare mage research and cold colonization in the middle game; then pursue unique expansion or regional unification according to the cult choice.
player_overview.overview: Eighard is a northern Autumn Court elven theocracy that once led a crusade against Winter but lost allies and prestige after its leader died. Restore cold-weather magic, develop northern outposts, and rebuild influence before facing the Cult of Rot's seizure of power: refusal opens a separate unification route, while acceptance gradually turns the country into Bannoghard. The clearest costs are long magical and colonial preparation and the cult's terror against prisoners and heretics.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy dark religious narratives, magical engineering, northern expansion, and national transformation.
signature_features: The Warming Ritual connects northern survival to cold-region expansion.
Accepting or refusing the Cult of Rot determines the later missions and formation eligibility.
The Rot route gradually turns an Autumn Court fortress into Bannoghard's terrifying religious state.
player_overview.tagline: Hold the cold coast with Autumn magic, then decide whether to hand the country to the Cult of Rot.

warnings: The 60 missions include mutually exclusive sections; simultaneous visibility is not promised.
The total cost, timers, and penalties of the third-stage magical projects are not fully checked or playtested.
Dedicated country Wiki coverage and Bannoghard history are missing; the later timeline is not an end-state guarantee.

positive_indicators: Cold-weather facilities and outposts protect residents
A political route exists that refuses the Cult of Rot
values.rationale: The primary score describes the distinctive Rot-extension route: the ideas explicitly place heretics and prisoners in pits until they die and rot, display bones as intimidation, and show the cult taking power through death threats. Cold-weather facilities provide public benefit but do not cancel concrete violations of personhood. The acceptance and refusal scores are alternative branches, not sequential stages: the refusal route can resist the cult, but later treatment of residents has not been fully checked, so it is not directly scored as Good. Autumn, theocracy, war, and decomposition magic are not penalized by themselves. Phase scores are editorial calibration, not script values.
red_flags: Prisoners and heretics are left to die and rot
Bones are displayed for terror rule
Power is seized through death threats that compel obedience
